check the code see it and find what to do next what is comptled like keel Every single benchmark duel—against Go, Swift, C (clang -O3), and Cargo—exposed specific, concrete bugs and bottlenecks rather than architectural flaws. Shipping a release (v0.3.2 / v0.3.3) that closes all of them will turn L++ from a strong prototype into an airtight daily-driver toolchain.

Here is the complete master checklist of everything discovered across your tests, grouped by system:

1. Critical Correctness & Reliability Bugs (Ship First)
False-Positive testing.assert_* (stdlib/testing.lpp): Currently, failed assertions print an error message and exit 0, causing keel test to report PASS. Make every assert_* / fail helper panic or call exit(1) immediately on failure.

main() -> Int Return Code Dropped in LLVM/Runtime Entrypoint: def main() -> Int: return 1 exits with OS status 0 instead of 1. Forward lpp_main()'s integer return value to the OS process exit code in the C/Rust runtime entrypoint.

Keel Workspace Dependency Import Failure (MissingModule): keel build stages local/registry dependencies under .lpp_packages/ and compiles their objects, but fails to pass those package search paths into lpp when compiling the root crate. Wire .lpp_packages/ module search paths and link dependency object artifacts into the final binary.

lppsqlite Multi-Process Lock Race (packages/lppsqlite): Update exec.acquire_lock from idempotent dir_create (create_dir_all) to your new exclusive file_open(lock_path, 2) (O_CREAT | O_EXCL / CREATE_NEW) flag with PID stale-lock recovery so concurrent processes cannot overwrite live snapshots.

2. Developer Experience & Diagnostics (Found in the UI/UX Audit)
Actionable UnresolvedName & Type Errors (crates/lpp-types): Print the missing identifier's exact name, file:line:col source snippet with a ^ underline, and a "did you mean '<closest_symbol>'?" suggestion instead of raw internal error tags.

keel check Caching & --check Mode: Hook keel check into Keel's fingerprint cache (bringing no-change checks from 651 ms down to < 10 ms) and add a --check flag to lpp so cold checks stop after type/ownership verification without running Cranelift/LLVM codegen.

First-Class --release / --backend Flags on keel: Expose keel build --release (mapping to --backend llvm -O3) and --backend cranelift|llvm natively so users don't need KEEL_LPP wrapper scripts.

3. Performance & Backend Parity Upgrades (Found in the C & Swift Duels)
LLVM --target-cpu=native / -march=native Flag (crates/lpp-codegen-llvm): Enable host-target CPU feature detection in TargetMachine so LLVM's LoopVectorizer and SLPVectorizer emit 256-bit AVX2/NEON instructions automatically on ordinary L++ loops (closing the 0.604 s vs. 0.260 s scalar checksum gap against clang -O3 -march=native).

Inline Fast-Path for Primitive List[Int] / List[Float] Indexing & push: Emit inline LLVM IR bounds-check + pointer load/store for primitive lists (calling lpp_list_grow only on capacity overflow) instead of crossing the dynamic PLT/GOT boundary on every element—cutting 30M-integer list loops from 0.343 s down to C's 0.168 s.

lppsqlite Read-Only close_db Optimization: Skip full-database file flushing in close_db when dirty == false so read-heavy HTTP workloads stop rewriting the entire database on GET requests.

WASM Str + scalar Parity & Char Interpolation: Bring crates/lpp-codegen-wasm's string concatenation in line with Cranelift/LLVM so f"{ch}" and Str + Int/Bool/Char compile identically across all backends.

4. Shared Library & Linking Polish (Found in the .so/.dll Audit)
Direct --shared / --dll CLI Flag on lpp: Forward --shared straight to lpp-link / host linker instead of requiring the two-step -c + manual link workflow.

PE Export Directory (.edata) in lpp-link (pe_writer.rs): Emit standard PE export tables for @export_name(...) functions and make DllMain optional under --shared so lpp-link builds standalone Windows .dll libraries without MSVC.

extern "C" link "<lib>" in LLVM Backend: Support extern "C" declarations in lpp-codegen-llvm alongside Cranelift so -O3 builds can link directly against libsqlite3 and C libraries.

5. Medium-Term Architectural Upgrades (v0.4 Roadmap)
Enforced Module Namespacing & pub Visibility (E3004): Replace flat global symbol resolution with module-scoped namespaces (pkg::mod::sym) so multi-package Keel projects never collide on internal helper names.

Non-Blocking OS I/O Reactor (epoll / kqueue / IOCP): Wire async socket readiness into TaskPool so network servers handle thousands of concurrent connections without pinning OS worker threads.

Remaining Syntax & SECURITY.md: Add nested match destructuring (Ok(Some((a, b)))), named struct construction (Point(x: 1.0, y: 2.0)), and a SECURITY.md + LICENSE cleanup in the repo root. and A test suit written in lpp of 40k loc that test alot

﻿# L++ Production-Grade Benchmark Results

Generated on **2026-07-16 22:02**
* **OS**: Microsoft Windows 10.0.26200 
* **CPU**: 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-1215U
* **C Compiler**: MSVC cl.exe (VS 2022 Community)
* **Rust Compiler**: rustc (opt-level=3)
* **Runs**: 3 (best-of)

---

## 1. Compiler Throughput (AOT mode: Source -> Native Executable)

This timing breakdown shows exactly where time is spent to build a fully linked native standalone executable from L++ source code.

| Benchmark | Frontend + MIR | Cranelift AOT | MSVC Linker | Total Compile time |
|-----------|----------------|---------------|-------------|--------------------|
| fib(35) | 1.9 ms | 1.5 ms | 390.3 ms | **393.7 ms** |
| loop(10M) | 1.8 ms | 1.4 ms | 102.3 ms | **105.5 ms** |
| calls(1M) | 13.2 ms | 12.6 ms | 219.3 ms | **245.1 ms** |

* **Frontend + MIR**: Lexer, Parser, Semantic Resolver, Typechecker, Escape Analysis, MIR conversion, and ARC pass.
* **Cranelift AOT**: Compiles MIR into machine instructions and writes COFF object bytes.
* **MSVC Linker**: Invokes Microsoft `link.exe` to link the object file with our precompiled static runtime `lpp_runtime.obj`.

---

## 2. Runtime Execution Benchmarks (Native Performance)

These figures demonstrate execution speed of the compiled binaries. L++ is compiled natively using the Cranelift AOT compiler.

| Benchmark | L++ Runtime (ms) | C Runtime (ms) | Rust Runtime (ms) | Python (ms) | Speedup vs Python | Correctness |
|-----------|------------------|----------------|-------------------|-------------|-------------------|-------------|
| fib(35) | 86 | 96.3 | 68 | 1444.8 | **16.8x** | PASS |
| loop(10M) | 43.3 | 64.3 | 66.1 | 910.6 | **21x** | PASS |
| calls(1M) | 51.8 | 34.2 | 36.5 | 222.3 | **4.3x** | PASS |

---

## 3. Native Executable Size Comparison

| Benchmark | L++ EXE Size | C EXE Size | Rust EXE Size |
|-----------|--------------|------------|---------------|
| fib(35) | **138 KB** | 137 KB | 123 KB |
| loop(10M) | **138 KB** | 137 KB | 123 KB |
| calls(1M) | **138 KB** | 137 KB | 123 KB |

### Why L++ Executables are extremely compact:
- Unlike **Rust**, L++ does not link a huge standard library (`std` in Rust defaults to linking backtrace, formatting systems, thread pools, and complex panic unwinding logic).
- Unlike **Python**, L++ compiles to machine code directly, requiring no VM or runtime interpreter to execute.

# L++ Roadmap — how complete is L++, and what "done" looks like

_Updated for **v0.3.2** (`v0.3-dev`). These figures and capabilities reflect
observed implementation and test suites in this tree; open items remain tracked
transparently below._

## 1. Completeness scorecard

## 2. Status since v0.2.0 & remaining build order

### Tier 1 — correctness & parity

1. ~~Cranelift structural-tuple drop glue~~ — **DONE**
   (`lpp_drop_t{n}`/`lpp_trace_t{n}`; see `docs/CYCLE_BREAKING.md`).
2. ~~WASM cycle collection~~ — **DONE.**
   `crates/lpp-codegen-wasm/src/cycle.rs` implements Bacon-Rajan trial-deletion
   cycle collection over `Shared` structs, enums, lists, tuples, closures, and
   tasks, bounded in memory across `cycle_gate` and 4-backend driver parity.
3. ~~LLVM managed-value, kernel, SIMD, and -O3 parity~~ — **DONE in v0.3.0.**
   `lpp-codegen-llvm` lowers full MIR, managed structs/enums/lists/tuples,
   cycle-collector ARC destructors, DWARF `-g`, SIMD intrinsics, kernel primitives,
   and `--backend llvm -O0`..`-O3`.
4. **Concurrency safety enforcement — PARTIAL.** `docs/CONCURRENCY.md`
   records the contract and open gaps. Add a concurrent-sharing fact to the
   ownership plan, enforce `Send`/`Sync` rules, add a collector-exclusion
   protocol, and validate under TSan.
5. ~~Stack-placed `Frame` POD & zero-overhead POD `Owned` codegen~~ — **DONE in v0.3.0.**
   `lpp-codegen-api::ownership_lowering` identifies non-escaping `Frame` POD
   structs/tuples for stack allocation (`StackSlot` / `alloca`) with zero ARC
   traffic, and passes null destructors for escaping POD `Owned` payloads across
   Cranelift and LLVM.

### Tier 2 — platform proof (S2 → S3)

6. **Windows MSVC proof — PARTIAL.** CI now executes the authored corpus,
   native compile/link/run, and PE smoke cases on `windows-latest`; it is no
   longer compile-only. Still add sanitizer-equivalent stale-handle/heap
   diagnostics for this toolchain and pin their results.
7. **macOS / aarch64 Linux proof — PARTIAL.** CI runs the corpus on macOS 14
   arm64 and macOS 15 Intel. aarch64 Linux runtime execution is still missing
   (and would close the linker `__libc_start_main` TODO).

### Tier 3 — language completeness

8. **Real async**: I/O readiness reactor (epoll/kqueue/IOCP adapters),
   backpressure, general suspension points, optional multi-thread executor.
9. **General slice lifetimes**: mutable slices, escapable views with
   lifetime parameters, slices across threads.
10. ~~Tuple parity and tuple arity beyond 4~~ — **DONE in v0.3.0**
    for Cranelift and LLVM (tuples up to arity 16 with managed elements).
11. **Iterator/generator protocol** — `Set[T]` and `Deque[T]` collections are **DONE in v0.3.0**; general lazy iterator/generator traits remain open.
12. **General auto-vectorization** of ordinary loops (`-O3` LLVM unlocks loop vectorization when eligible) and
    source-level wider SIMD types remain open. `vec_i64_checksum` dispatches to
    a 4-lane 256-bit AVX2 kernel with scalar fallback; this is workload-specific,
    not a general source-level `VectorI64x4` type (`benchmarks/simd/results.md`).
13. Macros/metaprogramming — *design decision required*, deliberately last:
    it multiplies the surface every other item must verify.

### Tier 4 — tooling & developer experience

14. ~~Debug info (DWARF `-g`) & runtime backtraces~~ — **DONE in v0.3.0**
    for Cranelift & LLVM, along with `lpp debug` CLI support. CodeView/WinDbg PDB emission remains open on Windows.
15. ~~`lpp fmt`, `lpp repl`, `lpp test`, `lpp/keel migrate`~~ — **DONE in v0.3.0.**
    LSP rename/references/code-actions remain open.
16. **In-repo fuzzing in CI** (seeded smoke: `scripts/fuzz_ownership.py
    --seed 1 --count 60`) and a one-command fast gate
    (`scripts/fast_gate.sh`). The fast gate now includes bindgen source
    compilation and a focused context-tombstone ASan/LSan/UBSan regression.

### Tier 5 — maturity (the long tail to 1.0)

17. Complete language specification (lifetimes, aliasing, FFI, unsafe
    boundary) — Safety Mission S4 prerequisite.
18. A **1.0 stability policy**: what may break, deprecation process, editions.
19. Independent security audit; formal/machine-checked soundness argument
    for the ownership core.
20. Ecosystem: hosted registry growth, docs hosting, more packages,
    production users. (Measured in years, not sprints — start early,
    finish last.)

**Sequencing rule:** features are *not* the bottleneck. Close Tier 1–2
before adding Tier-3 surface — every new syntax feature multiplies the
unverified area. A smaller language at S3 beats a bigger one at S2.
